analysis.title: Rates Spark: US midterms and expanding European government bond concerns
key_insights: Wednesday is the key day for Treasuries: US midterm election projections arrive Tuesday night and the Treasury refunding announcement follows on Wednesday.
The market's base case is Democrats taking the House and possibly the Senate. A blue sweep is seen as broadly discounted with little market impact.
ING says the only big surprise would be Republicans holding both chambers. That would probably be bond negative, on the view that it means more of the same until disproven.

On the refunding, ING sees either no change to the issuance profile or an indication that the Treasury has flexibility to cut long-end issuance later. Primary dealer questions a few weeks ago did not point to a big change.
ING does not think the Treasury needs to change course on issuance, because swap spreads are well-behaved. It would rather keep a change for when there is a material need to tighten swap spreads.
Fitch lowered the outlook on France's A+ rating to negative in an unscheduled review, citing weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit since the August review.
The 10y OAT/Bund spread still tightened about 4bp, in line with a broad tightening in government bond spreads that ING links to easing geopolitical tensions and oil coming off its highs.
ING notes France has traded like a BBB name for some time, so spreads are already wider than fundamentals alone would imply.

Belgian 10y spreads to Bunds widened by up to 4bp after the prime minister offered his resignation when the coalition failed to agree a budget. The King did not accept it immediately and will receive the prime minister on 6 November.
The Belgian central bank forecast a deficit of 5.3% for this year and 5.5% in 2027, and ING says fiscal consolidation is a problem beyond France.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Belgian central bank's summer forecast shows a wide deficit, which supports the view that France is not the only euro-area country struggling to consolidate its finances.
The deficit is forecast to widen further next year, which keeps Belgian spreads exposed to budget politics.
The outlook cut did not widen OAT/Bund. The spread tightened about 4bp.
This is the only scheduled US data before Friday's payrolls report.

risk_factors: Republicans holding both House and Senate would be a surprise and probably bond negative.
A refunding that signals lower long-end issuance flexibility could move the long end.
Fiscal consolidation problems in Belgium and France could widen euro-area government bond spreads.
A Belgian coalition failure on the budget could escalate if the King's 6 November meeting with the prime minister does not produce a compromise.
vol_and_positioning: ING says the market already discounts a Democratic House win and possibly a Senate win, so a blue sweep should have little impact.
ING says swap spreads are well-behaved, which argues against a Treasury change in issuance.
geopolitical: Easing geopolitical tensions and oil prices coming off their highs are cited as the driver of the broad tightening in European government bond spreads.
ING says a Republican hold of both chambers in the US midterms would suggest endorsement of the war, tariffs and current immigration policy.
The Belgian prime minister tendered his resignation after the coalition failed to agree a budget. The King called on the coalition parties to find a compromise.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic House, and possibly Senate, win is the market's base case and is broadly discounted, so a blue sweep should have little market impact.
tension_points.bear_case: A Republican hold of both chambers would be a big surprise and probably bond negative, as it would suggest an endorsement of the war, tariffs and current immigration policy and more of the same until disproven.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Election projections emerging Tuesday night that show Republicans holding both the House and the Senate.

tension_points.bull_case: ING expects no change to the issuance profile, or only an indication of flexibility to cut long-end issuance later, and says swap spreads are well-behaved.
tension_points.bear_case: There is growing talk of the refunding including a reduction in long-end issuance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Wednesday refunding announcement announcing an actual reduction in long-end issuance.

theme_stances.key_argument: A blue sweep is broadly discounted, while a Republican hold of both chambers would be a surprise and probably bond negative.
theme_stances.evidence: The more probable blue sweep should have little market impact

theme_stances.key_argument: Treasury does not need to change course on issuance because swap spreads are well-behaved.
theme_stances.evidence: We don't think the Treasury needs to panic here

theme_stances.key_argument: Belgium shows that France is not the only euro-area country struggling to consolidate its finances.
theme_stances.evidence: it is not only France that faces the challenge
